reason: This passage from Nehemiah 2 does not depict regular people complaining to their leaders, nor does it present a moral against such complaints. Instead, the text shows: (1) Nehemiah, an official, respectfully approaching King Artaxerxes with a request; (2) the Jewish people responding positively when called upon ('and they said, Let us rise up and build'); and (3) opposition from external enemies (Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem) being met with faith in God. The narrative concerns Nehemiah's mission to rebuild Jerusalem's walls and community mobilization, not commentary on whether common people should petition their leaders.
